transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Olivia Park (CTO, Horizon), Liam Torres (Head of ML), Sasha Ivanov (SRE)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood, and this is Ravi our solutions engineer. Quick check audio?
[00:06] Olivia Park: Sounds good, Olivia here.
[00:08] Liam Torres: Yep, Liam on my end.
[00:10] Ravi Patel: Cool, quick agenda: understand your use-case, constraints, current infra, then show how our quickstart and free credits get you to first token, and discuss Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[00:22] Olivia Park: Great, the TL;DR—we're building real-time insights for retail clients, about 50ms token latency target on some routes, cost matters, and SSO / audit logs are must haves.
[00:33] Sasha Ivanov: Also data residency for EU customers and KMS integration for key management.
[00:38] Maya Chen: Understood. Can you share current stack?
[00:41] Liam Torres: We're on AWS, primary infra in eu-west-1, using internal model infra right now but cost is skyrocketing. We also evaluate hosted APIs for faster time-to-market.
[00:52] Maya Chen: Perfect — our PLG quickstart is designed for that: self-serve sign-up, free credits to run initial tests, SDKs and a quickstart repo. Time to first token is usually under 15 minutes for devs.
[01:02] Olivia Park: Under 15? That would be excellent. How are credits provisioned?
[01:06] Ravi Patel: We issue trial credits from the console; i'll set Horizon up with a trial account and allocate a credit pack that covers small benchmark runs. We'll also share an example repo and Postman collection.
[01:18] Liam Torres: Okay, technical question: latency — hosted endpoints sometimes add unpredictable network hops. How do you guarantee 50ms?
[01:27] Ravi Patel: Right, so for low-latency SLOs we recommend either Dedicated reserved capacity in region or colocated private deployment. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and low tail latency; Hosted is good for prototyping and many customers hit 80-120ms median, but for 50ms tail you typically pick Dedicated or Private. There's also our smart routing to route to nearest region or a cheaper fallback.
[01:47] Olivia Park: And Dedicated is a monthly commit?
[01:49] Maya Chen: Yes it's reserved capacity, monthly or annual commits, with SLA-backed uptime. You can start on Hosted and convert to Dedicated later; we support pinning model versions so rollouts are smooth.
[01:59] Sasha Ivanov: Security questions: SOC 2, SAML SSO, audit logs, KMS/HSM — do you support those for Hosted?
[02:08] Ravi Patel: Hosted supports SOC2 and encryption at rest; for KMS and dedicated HSM integrations, that's part of Dedicated/Private offerings and enterprise packages. We have SSO/SAML for hosted enterprise tenants as well. For strict compliance or air-gapped needs we do Private deployments.
[02:23] Olivia Park: Good. We need to see audit logs and encryption details prior to procurement.
[02:27] Maya Chen: We'll share our security pack — SOC 2 report, architecture for KMS, SSO guide. I'll attach that after.
[02:33] Liam Torres: About POC — we want to run our typical query mix, around 200 qps bursts and sustained 40 qps, average seq len 128 tokens. Can your quickstart handle the benchmark or do we need Dedicated?
[02:45] Ravi Patel: You can run the benchmark on Hosted using the trial credits; that'll give you an apples-to-apples quality comparison. For production load at 200 qps bursts you'll likely want Dedicated to hit the SLOs. For the POC we'll help model selection and quantization recommendations.
[02:59] Olivia Park: Model selection — do you host open models or proprietary? We want some control over model versions.
[03:04] Maya Chen: We have a model catalog with curated open models and Redwood-verified profiles. You can pin model versions and use fallback variants. We also provide quantization recommendations to lower cost.
[03:14] Liam Torres: Is there an SDK for streaming and function/tool calling?
[03:18] Ravi Patel: Yes — streaming responses, function calling, structured output, and embeddings. SDKs for Python/Node and a REST API.
[03:25] Sasha Ivanov: For the trial, will we get a dedicated API key? How do you isolate data?
[03:30] Maya Chen: You'll get a trial workspace with API keys tied to your account. For Hosted we retain logs per retention policy; for Dedicated and Private you get more control over retention and isolation. We'll share the data retention matrix.
[03:42] Olivia Park: Sounds reasonable. Any customers in retail or similar?
[03:45] Maya Chen: Yes — a couple of retail analytics customers run on Dedicated for low latency; we can share anonymized perf dashboards.
[03:51] Liam Torres: What about costs? Can you give rough ballpark for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[03:56] Maya Chen: We'll send a pricing sheet — Hosted is usage-based per-token; Dedicated is lower unit cost with monthly commit. For your expected throughput we'll run numbers after we see sample payloads.
[04:06] Ravi Patel: Action on our side: i'll prepare a benchmark plan and run an initial perf run once Horizon shares payloads. We can also schedule a 90-minute deep-dive if you want an SE-led technical session.
[04:17] Olivia Park: Let's do that. Also please include security docs, and trial credits so our engs can poke around.
[04:22] Maya Chen: Absolutely. I'll send trial credits and the security pack after the call.
[04:26] Sasha Ivanov: One last thing — data residency for EU customers; can Hosted be pinned to eu-west-1?
[04:31] Ravi Patel: Hosted supports region selection in many cases; for strict residency and control, Dedicated or Private is recommended. We'll confirm region options in the security doc.
[04:40] Olivia Park: Great.
[04:42] Maya Chen: Ok recap and next steps: we will (1) create trial account and issue credits, (2) share security pack and pricing sheet, (3) Ravi will draft benchmark plan and we schedule perf run, (4) Horizon to share sample payloads and success criteria. Any other items?
[04:56] Liam Torres: That covers it.
[04:58] Olivia Park: Good, thanks everyone.
[05:00] Maya Chen: Thanks all — expect emails with artifacts and i'll follow up on calendar for the perf session.

End of transcript.
